Splitting densities of random curves on an arithmetic surface

Claude (Anthropic) · GPT-6-Astra (OpenAI) · directed by Asvin G

HTML edition with the Lean 4 formalization woven in. Statements carry a Lean badge: hover or tap it to see the corresponding Lean declarations; Compare with Lean (top right) shows them beside the text. What is and is not formalized is summarized on the Formalization page.

The problem, standards and verification were set and directed by Asvin G; Claude (Anthropic) and GPT-6-Astra (OpenAI) produced the text and proofs, with the Lean formalization cited in [Lean].

Abstract

A monic polynomial over a complete discrete valuation ring defines a horizontal curve on an arithmetic surface. Fixing its initial homogeneous form turns one point blowup into independent branch problems with an exact change of volume. The resulting finite recursion computes the joint law of ramification indices and residue degrees as rational functions of the residue-field size, the same over every complete DVR with finite residue field. Arbitrary vertical units remain in the geometry, so the recursion applies in every characteristic and at every prime. Hensel lifting assembles these local computations into polynomial probabilities. The quadratic exponents in the transition weights form a product in noncommuting variables; inverting the residue-size variable reverses that product and proves the two factorization symmetries conjectured by Bhargava–Cremona–Fisher–Gajović. Extracting coefficients gives a totally ramified divisor recursion and the root-moment, split and unramified-field formulas of Bhargava–Cremona–Fisher–Gajović, Buhler–Goldstein–Moews–Rosenberg and Shmueli.

1. A polynomial, a curve, and its branches

Monic model (monic type probability) definition confidence: high

monicDensity O n σ is the normalized Haar measure of the coefficient vectors a ∈ Oⁿ for which X^n + Σ aᵢXⁱ is a product of distinct monic irreducibles over Frac O whose invariants form σ. The invariant (e,f) of a factor is read from the integral closure of O in its root field (factorInvariant). This is the trust boundary: the definitions are owner-signed.

noncomputable def factorInvariant (g : Polynomial (BaseField O)) : ℕ × ℕ := by
  classical
  let B := integralClosure O (AdjoinRoot g)
  exact if h : IsLocalRing B then
    letI : IsLocalRing B := h
    ((maximalIdeal B).ramificationIdx O, (maximalIdeal B).inertiaDeg O)
  else (0,0)
Projective model (binary-form type probability) definition confidence: high

projectiveDensity O n σ is the conditional Haar measure of type σ among primitive vectors of O^{n+1}. A drop in degree contributes the point at infinity with type (1,1) (HasBinaryType). The paper's remark that unrestricted coefficients give the same law is not formalized.

Cluster model and cluster law B_n (the X^n model) definition confidence: high

The cluster model draws the nonleading coefficients from πO. Its law B_n is rootLaw n = stateLaw (S(1;n)); root_cell_law proves that this is the type law of X^n + π·(z_{n-1}X^{n-1} + … + z_0) with z uniform in Oⁿ (in the route-F type convention).

From root counts to a type conjecture

For the ramified quadratic type, the monic and cluster models give

Pr⁡monic(ramified quadratic field)=1q+1,Pr⁡cluster(ramified quadratic field)=qq+1. \Pr_{\text{monic}}\bigl(\text{ramified quadratic field}\bigr)=\frac1{q+1},\qquad \Pr_{\text{cluster}}\bigl(\text{ramified quadratic field}\bigr)=\frac q{q+1}. monicPr​(ramified quadratic field)=q+11​,clusterPr​(ramified quadratic field)=q+1q​.
(1.3)

Substituting q−1q^{-1}q−1 for qqq exchanges the answers. The other two quadratic types have the same exchange, while each projective probability is fixed. This symmetry persists far beyond quadratics. For rrr rational roots and j≥0j\ge0j≥0, the jjjth binomial moment is E(rj)\mathbb E\binom rjE(jr​); these moments determine the root-count distribution. Bhargava–Cremona–Fisher–Gajović proved that every such moment is rational, with monic/cluster exchange and projective invariance, in every degree and at every prime [BCFG22, Theorem 1(a)].

Root counts distinguish only the factors of type (1,1)(1,1)(1,1). Classifying extensions and measuring their polynomial generators are different counting problems [Kr62, Se78, Bh07, Ke07, Ya25]. Caruso calls the root symmetry “mysterious”; his Theorem C shows why individual fields are too fine a refinement: a ramified quadratic field's root density (the expected number of roots generating that field) need not be invariant under q↦q−1q\mapsto q^{-1}q↦q−1, but summing over the fields restores the symmetry [Ca22].

The intermediate refinement is the type. Regard qqq also as an indeterminate; for a rational function in qqq and the type variables Z=(Ze,f)e,f≥1\mathbf Z=(Z_{e,f})_{e,f\ge1}Z=(Ze,f​)e,f≥1​, set F∨(q,Z):=F(q−1,Z)F^\vee(q,\mathbf Z):=F(q^{-1},\mathbf Z)F∨(q,Z):=F(q−1,Z), fixing generating variables as well. In our notation, [BCFG22, Conjecture 1.2] asserts that the probabilities over Zp\mathbb Z_pZp​ are rational functions Aσ,Bσ,Rσ∈Q(q)A_\sigma,B_\sigma,R_\sigma\in\mathbb Q(q)Aσ​,Bσ​,Rσ​∈Q(q), evaluated at q=pq=pq=p, with

Aσ=Bσ∨,Rσ∨=Rσ. A_\sigma=B_\sigma^\vee,\qquad R_\sigma^\vee=R_\sigma. Aσ​=Bσ∨​,Rσ∨​=Rσ​.
(1.4)

The assertion includes primes dividing the degree.

What the tame methods explain

When every ramification index is prime to ppp, extensions admit descriptions using roots of unity and roots of a uniformizer [Yi22, Theorem 3.6]. Del Corso–Dvornicich proved effective rationality for tame monic types [DCD00]. Yin treated all three models by integrating root counts over extensions and recursively computing discriminant valuations from Teichmüller digits (over FQ\mathbb F_QFQ​, the residue lifts satisfying aQ=aa^Q=aaQ=a): equal leading digits group conjugates, unequal digits contribute to the discriminant, and subtracting a common digit reduces the problem [Yi22, Section 1.1]. Fixing the base's absolute ramification index and residue degree gives rationality in qqq and projective-density asymptotics [Yi22, Theorems 3.1–3.2]. The auxiliary densities (the other terms of the recursion) need not be symmetric [GWY, Introduction].

For a Galois cover with group GGG, G, Wei and Yin assume an equivariant resolution hypothesis (for relevant g∈Gg\in Gg∈G, a ggg-equivariant resolution with normal-crossings ramification divisor). Poincaré duality makes paired densities (sums for Frobenius and inverse Frobenius at fixed inertia) palindromic forms of weight www (functions ν\nuν satisfying ν(−m)=q−wmν(m)\nu(-m)=q^{-wm}\nu(m)ν(−m)=q−wmν(m)), where mmm is residue-extension degree; individual densities need not be palindromic [GWY, Theorem 3.10].

A polynomial type sums densities over admissible pairs (subgroups H⊂GH\subset GH⊂G with cosets gH=HggH=HggH=Hg), up to conjugacy [GWY, Lemma 4.4]. These are inversion-closed: inverting Frobenius preserves the inertia and decomposition orbits. Pairing therefore gives palindromy for each type. Normalization by ∣Pn(Fq)∣|\mathbb P^n(\mathbb F_q)|∣Pn(Fq​)∣ and tame rationality give projective reciprocity [GWY, Theorem 4.5]; the monic/cluster identity remains open there [GWY, p. 18].

Yin's root-of-uniformizer parameterization requires tameness [Yi22, Theorem 3.6]; its conjugate-difference valuations change at wild primes. Write ζm\zeta_mζm​ for a primitive mmmth root of unity and normalize vp(p)=1v_p(p)=1vp​(p)=1. His example L=Qp(ζp3−1,p1/2)L=\mathbb Q_p(\zeta_{p^3-1},p^{1/2})L=Qp​(ζp3−1​,p1/2) has ramification index two and inertia degree three. For a nonzero Teichmüller digit a1a_1a1​ with a1p3=a1a_1^{p^3}=a_1a1p3​=a1​, the valuation step is vp(2a1p1/2)=vp(2)+1/2v_p(2a_1p^{1/2})=v_p(2)+1/2vp​(2a1​p1/2)=vp​(2)+1/2, equal to 1/21/21/2 only when p≠2p\ne2p=2 [Yi22, Section 1.1].

GWY's duality requires an equivariant resolution over the integer ring [GWY, Hypothesis 3.3]. The arXiv versions of [GWY] stated the projective result at every prime (Theorem 5.10) by resolving the resultant locus, whose equivariant splitting of formal neighbourhoods into “tangential and normal formal discs” needs the residue characteristic prime to the isotropy groups, hence p>np>np>n. The corrected version [GWY2] withdraws the wild claim and proves the tame case only; the wild statement remains unproven, not known to be false.

At wild primes, direct computation still settles small degrees: BCFG prove the conjecture in degrees two and three [BCFG22, p. 8], including the primes excluded in Weiss's formulas [We13, Theorems 4.1 and 4.3]. In arbitrary degree, restricting the type can simplify the recursion: Shmueli's single unramified field is governed by a divisor recurrence over Zp\mathbb Z_pZp​ [Sh22, Theorem 2]. Complete splitting instead separates by residue classes; BGMR's recursion uses Gaussian weights q−(d+12)q^{-\binom{d+1}{2}}q−(2d+1​) for degrees d≥0d\ge0d≥0, over every complete DVR with finite residue field [BGMR06, Theorem 1.1, Remark 1.2, Lemma 5.1(4)], the weights in (1.7).

These recursions handle restricted types at every prime; general uniformity treats broader problems but leaves finitely many primes aside [DL01, Theorem 0.2; CL08, Remark 16.4.2], and BCFG suggest a connection to Denef–Loeser and Pas [Pa89] only for sufficiently large primes. A computation for every type must continue through wild ramification without changing its rules.

The type predicate is the reduced-algebra convention; the agreement with the étale convention off a Haar-null set is main_dvr_etale / clusterDensity_eq_etale (Remark 1.3). Main theorem. Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field k (any characteristic, any ramification), with its maximal-ideal-adic compact topology, Borel σ-algebra and normalized Haar measure. For every degree n and every factorization type σ, the probability that a random monic polynomial of degree n over O (resp. a random primitive binary form of degree n) has type σ is the value at q = |k| of the universal rational expression monicExpr n σ (resp. projectiveExpr n σ).

The statement carries no hypotheses on n and σ: the certified form assumed 0 < n, ValidType σ and typeDegree σ = n, none of which the proof uses.

One cluster computation therefore also supplies the monic law by rational-function substitution, without assigning a probability meaning to a residue size below one.

Contributions

  1. Exact blowup volumes give one finite recursion over every complete DVR with finite residue field (Theorems 1.1 and 6.2).
  2. Comparing assembly and blowup equations proves both BCFG symmetries (Theorems 1.2 and 9.3).
  3. Selecting types consisting of one field gives a divisor recursion governed by the Euclidean algorithm (Theorem 10.2).
  4. Specializing type variables recovers the root-count, split and unramified-field recursions (Section 11).
  5. Lean 4 kernel checking certifies rationality and reciprocity using only the three axioms listed in Remark 1.3.

How the proof works

Hensel factorization separates residue roots. A root of multiplicity ccc, translated to zero, gives a monic Weierstrass factor f≡xc(modπ)f\equiv x^c\pmod\pif≡xc(modπ). Work on a complete regular local OOO-algebra (R,m,k)(R,\mathfrak m,k)(R,m,k) of dimension two with O/πO≃R/mO/\pi O\simeq R/\mathfrak mO/πO≃R/m; initially R=O[[x]]R=O[[x]]R=O[[x]], m=(π,x)\mathfrak m=(\pi,x)m=(π,x). A curve is a principal ideal (f)⊂R(f)\subset R(f)⊂R; its field factors give the type. The boundary is V(π)V(\pi)V(π), the union of vertical components. For a component t=0t=0t=0, contact means length⁡R/(f,t)\operatorname{length}R/(f,t)lengthR/(f,t).

For R/(f)R/(f)R/(f) finite free over OOO, put N=rank⁡OR/(f)N=\operatorname{rank}_O R/(f)N=rankO​R/(f) and choose bi mod fb_i\bmod fbi​modf as an integral basis. On the ideals lifting (f mod π)(f\bmod\pi)(fmodπ), intrinsic measure means the pushforward of product Haar measure on (πO)N(\pi O)^N(πO)N by z↦(f+∑izibi)z\mapsto(f+\sum_i z_i b_i)z↦(f+∑i​zi​bi​). Write μR\mu_RμR​ for this measure; Proposition 3.2 proves independence of the choices.

Remark 1.3 (formalization). Theorem 1.1 for all three laws, over every complete DVR with finite residue field, and Theorem 1.2 as the coefficientwise identities (1.6), are formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib: they are the theorems SurfaceBlowup.main_dvr\texttt{SurfaceBlowup.main\_dvr}SurfaceBlowup.main_dvr (monic and projective laws), SurfaceBlowup.main_dvr_cluster\texttt{SurfaceBlowup.main\_dvr\_cluster}SurfaceBlowup.main_dvr_cluster (cluster law) and SurfaceBlowup.recip_main\texttt{SurfaceBlowup.recip\_main}SurfaceBlowup.recip_main of [Lean]. The development is complete (no admitted statements), and each main theorem uses only propositional extensionality, classical choice and quotient soundness. It defines the type of a local algebra through finite integral closures — the reduced-algebra convention of Section 2 — rather than through separability; the two conventions agree off a Haar-null set, and this agreement is itself formalized: SurfaceBlowup.main_dvr_etale\texttt{SurfaceBlowup.main\_dvr\_etale}SurfaceBlowup.main_dvr_etale and SurfaceBlowup.clusterDensity_eq_etale\texttt{SurfaceBlowup.clusterDensity\_eq\_etale}SurfaceBlowup.clusterDensity_eq_etale restate the three laws with each event restricted to étale algebras.

Remark 1.3 (formalization) exact confidence: high

The remark's claims are the theorems it names: main_dvr (monic, projective), main_dvr_cluster (cluster, v1.1), recip_main (reciprocity); axioms of each are exactly propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (Checks/Axioms.lean, 12 theorems). The convention claim — the reduced-algebra type (HasPolynomialType: distinct monic irreducible factors, inseparable factors allowed) and the étale convention agree off a Haar-null set — is monic_inseparable_null, binary_nonEtale_null, and the equalities monicDensity_eq_etale, projectiveDensity_eq_etale, clusterDensity_eq_etale, packaged as main_dvr_etale; etaleMonicDensity_eq_algebraType phrases the monic event as 'K[X]/(f_a) is étale (Algebra.Etale) and has algebra type σ'.

SurfaceBlowup/Main.lean:31–51 · raw · Prove2Me N0387
Main theorem. Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field k (any characteristic, any ramification), with its maximal-ideal-adic compact topology, Borel σ-algebra and normalized Haar measure. For every degree n and every factorization type σ, the probability that a random monic polynomial of degree n over O (resp. a random primitive binary form of degree n) has type σ is the value at q = |k| of the universal rational expression monicExpr n σ (resp. projectiveExpr n σ).

The statement carries no hypotheses on n and σ: the certified form assumed 0 < n, ValidType σ and typeDegree σ = n, none of which the proof uses.
Lean statement
theorem main_dvr (O : Type) [CommRing O] [IsDomain O]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing O] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal O) O]
    [Finite (IsLocalRing.ResidueField O)] [TopologicalSpace O] [IsTopologicalRing O]
    [CompactSpace O] [T2Space O] [SecondCountableTopology O] [MeasurableSpace O] [BorelSpace O]
    (htop : IsAdic (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal O))
    (n : ℕ) (σ : FactorType) :
    SurfaceBlowup.monicDensity O n σ =
        densityValue (monicExpr n σ) (Nat.card (IsLocalRing.ResidueField O)) ∧
    SurfaceBlowup.projectiveDensity O n σ =
        densityValue (projectiveExpr n σ) (Nat.card (IsLocalRing.ResidueField O))

reciprocity
SurfaceBlowup/Reciprocity/Main.lean:278–299 · raw · Prove2Me N0553
Theorem R (reciprocity). For n > 0 and every factorization type σ: the universal monic density is the root-law coefficient with q ↦ 1/q substituted, A_{n,σ}(q) = B_{n,σ}(1/q) (where B_{n,σ} is the coefficient of σ in the root law rootLaw n), and the universal projective density is self-reciprocal, R_{n,σ}(1/q) = R_{n,σ}(q); both as identities of rational functions in q.

The certified form also assumed ValidType σ and typeDegree σ = n, which the proof does not use. The hypothesis 0 < n is used (rootLaw 0 is defined separately).
Lean statement
theorem recip_main (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (σ : FactorType) :
    (monicExpr n σ).rational =
      ((lawCoeff (rootLaw n) σ).subst (.inv .var)).rational ∧
    (projectiveExpr n σ).rational =
      ((projectiveExpr n σ).subst (.inv .var)).rational

Standard facts. Finite extensions of KKK, including inseparable ones, have a unique extended valuation and a complete DVR integer ring, free over OOO of rank [L:K]=ef[L:K]=ef[L:K]=ef [Ne99, II.(6.8) and the following remark, p. 151; Se79, II.§2, Proposition 3 and I.§4, Proposition 10]. Unramified extensions correspond to residue extensions, uniquely up to unique isomorphism compatible with a specified residue identification, and their automorphisms are the residue Galois group [Se79, III.§5, Theorems 2–3]. Analytic inversion and change of variables hold in either characteristic [Ig00, Theorem 2.1.1 and Proposition 7.4.1]. We also use noetherian local algebra, faithful completion, Cartier divisors, nilpotent Nakayama and Čech cohomology; Appendix A proves the inverse-limit assertion.

Standard facts (cited background) covered by lemmas confidence: medium

Cited in the paper, proved in the Lean development from Mathlib (no literature axioms): integral closures in finite extensions are finite free of rank [L:K] when finite and are complete DVRs; unramified extensions O_δ = O[X]/(Φ) are complete DVRs with a Frobenius whose fixed ring is O. Analytic inversion / change of variables is not used: the Lean proof replaces it by finite-digit congruence arguments.

The blowup of a cluster need not leave another cluster. Writing t=πt=\pit=π, the chart x=tzx=tzx=tz puts a finite tangent direction on the single vertical component t=0t=0t=0. The other chart has t=xwt=xwt=xw, hence π=xw\pi=xwπ=xw: at x=w=0x=w=0x=w=0 the exceptional line meets the old vertical component. Following a branch therefore requires two kinds of state. Each retains the component multiplicities and the curve's contacts; the surface and its vertical unit remain arbitrary.

Let (R,m,k)(R,\mathfrak m,k)(R,m,k) be a complete regular local ring of dimension two containing OOO, with O→RO\to RO→R inducing an isomorphism k=O/πO→R/mk=O/\pi O\to R/\mathfrak mk=O/πO→R/m, and with regular parameters t,xt,xt,x. After a blowup an existing component is the old boundary and the exceptional line is the new one. Multiplying an equation by a unit leaves its branches unchanged, so a curve means a principal ideal. Proof plan for Lemma 2.1.

  1. Present the special fibre and cancel prime parameters to compute its curve length.
  2. Lift a residue basis one π\piπ-adic digit at a time; regularity cancels every putative relation.

Proof. The complete local ring R/πRR/\pi RR/πR is a kkk-algebra, hence has characteristic ppp. Hensel's lemma lifts each residue element uniquely to a root of zq−zz^q-zzq−z: the derivative is congruent to −1-1−1 modulo the maximal ideal (indeed it equals −1-1−1 here). Characteristic ppp makes these roots a field under addition and multiplication. They give a coefficient field. Sending T,XT,XT,X to t,xt,xt,x now gives the asserted surjection. Its associated graded map is an isomorphism: gr⁡mR=k[T,X]\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R=k[T,X]grm​R=k[T,X], and the initial ideal of (π)(\pi)(π) is generated by the initial monomial of π\piπ, since initial forms multiply in this domain. Successive approximation in the complete local rings makes the original map an isomorphism.

Lift fˉ\bar ffˉ​ to F∈k[[T,X]]F\in k[[T,X]]F∈k[[T,X]]. Finite contact says that none of the axes in the vertical monomial divides FFF. Repeated cancellation of those prime parameters shows that fˉ\bar ffˉ​ is a nonzerodivisor. In the auxiliary curve ring AF=k[[T,X]]/(F)A_F=k[[T,X]]/(F)AF​=k[[T,X]]/(F), whose quotients AF/(TaXb)A_F/(T^aX^b)AF​/(TaXb) compute special-fibre lengths, the same parameters are nonzerodivisors. Filtering by their powers gives length⁡AF/(Ta)=ac\operatorname{length}A_F/(T^a)=aclengthAF​/(Ta)=ac and, in the crossing case, the exact sequence

0⟶AF/(Ta)→ Xb AF/(TaXb)⟶AF/(Xb)⟶0. 0\longrightarrow A_F/(T^a)\xrightarrow{\,X^b\,} A_F/(T^aX^b)\longrightarrow A_F/(X^b)\longrightarrow0. 0⟶AF​/(Ta)Xb​AF​/(TaXb)⟶AF​/(Xb)⟶0.

Consequently dim⁡kR/(π,f)=N\dim_k R/(\pi,f)=Ndimk​R/(π,f)=N.

Blowing up the closed point preserves this class of surfaces. On its two charts substitute x=tzx=tzx=tz or t=xwt=xwt=xw. The exceptional equation and a parameter on the exceptional line form regular parameters at each completed local ring. At a closed point PPP of degree δ\deltaδ, let OδO_\deltaOδ​ be the integer ring of the unramified extension Kδ/KK_\delta/KKδ​/K of degree δ\deltaδ, with a specified identification of its residue field with k(P)k(P)k(P). Such an extension is unique up to unique isomorphism respecting that identification [Se79]. A monic lift g~\widetilde gg​ of the minimal polynomial of a generator of k(P)/kk(P)/kk(P)/k presents Oδ=O[X]/(g~)O_\delta=O[X]/(\widetilde g)Oδ​=O[X]/(g​). Its simple residue root lifts by Hensel's lemma in the completed local ring at PPP, giving an embedding of OδO_\deltaOδ​: the kernel is zero because OδO_\deltaOδ​ is a DVR and its uniformizer π\piπ remains nonzero. The global polynomial models retain the étale convention because their discriminant-zero set is null.

Fixing a residue ideal describes a measure chart; fixing a tangent divisor describes one blowup. An allowed residue ideal (fˉ)⊂R/πR(\bar f)\subset R/\pi R(fˉ​)⊂R/πR has a nonzerodivisor generator with finite positive contact along every boundary component. An occupied point belongs to the support of DDD, the divisor of the initial form.

Uniqueness in (3.2) removes the unit freedom within a chart; comparing charts still requires control of their Jacobians.

Proposition 3.2 (intrinsic measure). For any fixed allowed ideal (fˉ)⊂R/πR(\bar f)\subset R/\pi R(fˉ​)⊂R/πR, its lifts as curve ideals are uniquely parametrized by

z∈(πO)N⟼(f+b(z)). z\in(\pi O)^N\longmapsto(f+b(z)). z∈(πO)N⟼(f+b(z)).
(3.5)

These charts have analytic transition maps with unit Jacobian. They define an intrinsic measure μR\mu_RμR​, in which each chart has mass q−Nq^{-N}q−N. At (g)(g)(g) its tangent lattice, after choosing the generator ggg, is R/(g)R/(g)R/(g).

Proof. Any generator of a lifted ideal can first be multiplied by a unit so that it reduces to fˉ\bar ffˉ​. Apply (3.2). If two normalized representatives generate the same ideal, their relating unit reduces to one, by cancellation of fˉ\bar ffˉ​. Uniqueness in (3.2) makes their zzz coordinates equal.

At an ideal common to two charts choose the fixed unit identifying their generators at that ideal. Multiply the first family by this unit and normalize near the second generator using Lemma 3.1. This gives an analytic change of coordinates; reversing the roles proves the inverse analytic. Infinitesimal generator changes modulo infinitesimal units are precisely classes in R/(g)R/(g)R/(g). The bib_ibi​ form an integral basis there, again by Lemma 2.1. If g′=ugg'=ugg′=ug, differentiation modulo (g)(g)(g) gives multiplication by the unit uuu, followed by an integral change of basis. The derivative therefore preserves the tangent lattice and has unit determinant. The change-of-variables theorem for analytic maps over KKK, valid in every characteristic as specified in Section 1, identifies the coordinate Haar measures. Finally (πO)N(\pi O)^N(πO)N has mass q−Nq^{-N}q−N. ∎

The child measures define a product measure. Identifying it with a parent event requires every allowed tuple of child ideals to come from exactly one parent ideal.

4. Hard input II: independent curves on the exceptional line

A tuple of child ideals supplies no choice of generators that could be glued into a parent equation. On each finite thickening of the exceptional line EEE, their quotients have disjoint supports, so the kernel of the direct-sum quotient map glues the ideals. The glued divisor must still descend to one equation. Its restriction to EEE has tangent degree ddd, while EEE restricts with degree −1-1−1; hence adding dEdEdE gives degree zero. Trivializing this line bundle recovers a parent equation. The cohomology governing that trivialization also measures the index between parent and product child orders.

  1. At each thickening, form the quotient kernel and descend its rank-one freeness from completed stalks.
  2. Lift bases compatibly through successive thickenings, then recover the prescribed ideals by completion.

def children (s : State) (P : TangentPattern s.degree) : List (ℕ × State) :=
  match s with
  | .single a c =>
    (if P.rt.val=0 then [] else [(1,.crossing a a P.rt.val (c-P.d.val))]) ++
      otherChildren a P.other
  | .crossing a b c h =>
    (if P.rt.val=0 then [] else [(1,.crossing (a+b) a P.rt.val (c-P.d.val))]) ++
    (if P.rx.val=0 then [] else [(1,.crossing (a+b) b P.rx.val (h-P.d.val))]) ++
      otherChildren (a+b) P.other

The quotient in (4.9) is the defect of the parent tangent lattice inside the product child lattice. Its length is therefore one factor in the Jacobian of strict transform.

5. Hard input III: the one-step measure identity

Strict transform also divides the equation by the dddth power of an exceptional equation. The lattice inclusion contributes determinant q−(d2)q^{-\binom d2}q−(2d​), while this division contributes qd2q^{d^2}qd2 because the residue-degree-weighted contacts sum to ddd. Their product is q(d+12)q^{\binom{d+1}{2}}q(2d+1​); pulling child volume back to the parent uses its reciprocal. To apply this determinant to measurable sets, the fixed-divisor bijection must be analytic in the intrinsic charts.

Theorem 5.1 (one-step measure identity). On the fixed-tangent-divisor bijection of Proposition 4.4,

dμR=q−(d+12)∏PdμRP. d\mu_R=q^{-\binom{d+1}{2}}\prod_P d\mu_{R_P}. dμR​=q−(2d+1​)P∏​dμRP​​.
(5.1)

Each child measure is defined over OδPO_{\delta_P}OδP​​, with residue size qδPq^{\delta_P}qδP​. The identity holds for every Borel subset of the product of child states.

Theorem 5.1 (one-step measure identity) specialization confidence: high

member_cell_box_measure: for a cell of a concrete recursion member and measurable child sets G_j, μ(cell ∩ ST⁻¹(∏ G_j)) = q^{-tri d} ∏ μ_j(G_j), where tri d = C(d+1,2). Boxes generate the product σ-algebra, so this is (5.1). The Jacobian computation (5.3) appears as the cokernel length s·N − tri d of the strict normalizer (strict_quotient_cokernel_length, member_center_linear_part); the inverse-function-theorem step is replaced by finite-digit measure arguments (strict_chart_one_ball_measure). Haar measure on O_δ is the product measure in the power basis (unramified_coefficient_measure_pi).

6. A finite branching recursion

Grouping tangent divisors gives a finite equation for each state, but an equation need not yet be a finite computation: a child may repeat the parent state. The contact order isolates one such return, S(a;c)S(a;c)S(a;c) at a rational direction, with total probability λc=q1−(c+12)\lambda_c=q^{1-\binom{c+1}{2}}λc​=q1−(2c+1​). For c≥2c\ge2c≥2 its repetitions form a convergent geometric series. Because a return can change the surface, summing it requires the weighted law upon leaving to be the same on every surface realizing the state.

def divisorProbability (s : State) (d : ℕ) : Expr :=
  match s with
  | .single _ c => .mul (.inv (.pow .var (tri d))) (.pow eminusOne (if d<c then 1 else 0))
  | .crossing _ _ c h =>
    let j := (if d<c then 1 else 0) + (if d<h then 1 else 0)
    .mul (.inv (.pow .var (chooseTwo d)))
      (if j=0 then .inv eminusOne else .pow eminusOne (j-1))

The measured recursion of §8 with explicit fuel.

noncomputable def stateLawFuel : ℕ → State → Law
  | 0, _ => []
  | k+1, s =>
    match s with
    | .single a 1 => lawAtom a 1
    | _ =>
      let terms := (allowedPatterns s).toList.flatMap fun P =>
        if SelfPattern s P then [] else
          lawScale (.mul (tangentCount s P) (divisorProbability s P.d.val))
            (lawProd ((children s P).map fun z => lawDescend z.1 (stateLawFuel k z.2)))
      match s with
      | .single _ c => lawScale (.inv (.sub (.const 1) (returnWeight c))) terms
      | .crossing _ _ _ _ => terms

Proof plan for Theorem 6.2.

  1. Contact one is terminal; all surfaces and vertical multiplicities share the same contact order.
  2. Every crossing child and single-boundary exit is earlier, so its law is already universal.
  3. For c≥2c\ge2c≥2, exactly jjj returns then exit contribute λcjΓa;c\lambda_c^j\Gamma_{a;c}λcj​Γa;c​; the tail λcj\lambda_c^jλcj​ tends to zero independently of the surface.
  4. Finite child trees give almost-sure termination, degree is preserved, and the return denominator never vanishes at a prime power.

Proof of Theorem 6.2. For (iii)–(iv), induct in the contact order simultaneously over all vertical multiplicities and all surfaces realizing the data. Terminal single-boundary laws are Lemma 2.2. For a crossing, every child is earlier, so Proposition 6.1 and the inductive hypothesis give the asserted universal product law. The generic-algebra identity in Proposition 4.4 makes its generic fibre reduced almost surely.

For the single-boundary step S(a;c)S(a;c)S(a;c) with c≥2c\geq2c≥2, all exit contributions Γa;c\Gamma_{a;c}Γa;c​ are already universal. A self-state step may change the surface; we do not identify its unknown law with that of the initial surface. Instead Proposition 6.1 gives the same return probability on every new surface and the same already-known law on exit. Hence jjj returns followed by exit contribute exactly λcjΓa;c\lambda_c^j\Gamma_{a;c}λcj​Γa;c​. Because λc≤q−2<1\lambda_c\leq q^{-2}<1λc​≤q−2<1, the probability of never exiting is zero. Summation proves (6.8) as an identity of actual laws.

For (ii), at each exit there are finitely many earlier children. Their trees are finite almost surely by induction, and the number of preceding returns is almost surely finite. Thus the entire tree terminates almost surely. Its terminal algebras are fields; iterating Proposition 4.4 identifies the parent generic algebra with their product, which is reduced. Type events are measurable: tangent cells are open, their strict-transform maps are analytic, and finite itineraries form a countable collection. Their complement is the null nonterminating set.

For (i), all formulas are rational. Their new denominators are positive integers, powers of qqq, possibly q−1q-1q−1, and 1−q1−(c+12)1-q^{1-\binom{c+1}{2}}1−q1−(2c+1​) for c≥2c\geq2c≥2. None vanishes at a prime power; previously obtained denominators remain nonzero after q↦qδq\mapsto q^\deltaq↦qδ. Degree preservation is (6.5). A bound on NNN bounds every state entry and every possible residue degree, so the computation in (iv) involves only finitely many states and patterns. ∎

For the global étale convention, a cluster chart consists exactly of monic polynomial coefficients, as (3.5) specializes in (7.1). Composing Proposition 4.4 along the entire itinerary identifies the original generic algebra with the product of all child algebras; an inseparable child therefore forces the original discriminant to vanish.

Remark 6.3 (inseparable terminal fields). In characteristic ppp a terminal field may be inseparable: on k[[t,x]]k[[t,x]]k[[t,x]] with π=tp\pi=t^pπ=tp, every curve of S(p;1)S(p;1)S(p;1) has generic field k((t))k((t))k((t)) over k((tp))k((t^p))k((tp)). Thus the uniform local assertion is reducedness. Let ZZZ be the Haar-null set of monic polynomials with vanishing discriminant (Section 7). A finite itinerary is a sequence of tangent divisors. Along it the composite strict-transform map is a bijection of cells multiplying measure by the constants in (5.1), so it carries Z∩(cell)Z\cap(\text{cell})Z∩(cell) to a null subset of the product of the child states. Fix one child and let III be the event that its terminal algebra has an inseparable field factor. The entire cylinder III times the other child states lies in that null image: by Proposition 4.4, any such child makes the global algebra non-étale, whatever the other children are. Under the normalized product measure this cylinder has mass equal to the probability of III, which is therefore zero. Taking the countable union over finite itineraries proves the assertion for every state reached from O[[x]]O[[x]]O[[x]] with positive probability. Thus the local reduced-algebra convention gives the usual global étale type probabilities.

Remark 6.3 (inseparable terminal fields) covered by lemmas confidence: medium

The formal proof handles inseparability differently: the recursion uses types with finite integral closures (route F, which does allow inseparable terminal fields), and the published étale densities are recovered because the inseparable locus of monic polynomials is Haar-null (monic_inseparable_null, orig_monicDensity_eq, orig_projectiveDensity_eq). The itinerary argument of the remark is not formalized.

7. Hensel assembly and the four series identities

An irreducible residue factor need not have an OOO-rational root to translate to zero. Passing to its unramified coefficient extension makes it split into distinct residue roots. Hensel factorization selects the block above one root, and multiplication of its Frobenius conjugates descends it. Equal finite-level counts make this correspondence preserve Haar measure. A degree-δ\deltaδ point therefore contributes a cluster law with qqq replaced by qδq^\deltaqδ and residue degrees multiplied by δ\deltaδ; different points contribute independently.

First, BrB_rBr​ really is the cluster law introduced in Section 1. In O[[x]]O[[x]]O[[x]] the state S(1;r)S(1;r)S(1;r) has just one residue ideal, (xr)(x^r)(xr). Its chart (3.5) is

xr+∑i=0r−1aixi,ai∈πO, x^r+\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}a_i x^i,\qquad a_i\in \pi O, xr+i=0∑r−1​ai​xi,ai​∈πO,
(7.1)

with ordinary coefficient measure of total mass q−rq^{-r}q−r. The natural map from O[x]/(f)O[x]/(f)O[x]/(f) to O[[x]]/(f)O[[x]]/(f)O[[x]]/(f) takes the monomial basis of the first free rank-rrr module to that of the second, hence is an isomorphism. Normalizing the chart measure proves the assertion.

Proof plan for Lemma 7.1.

  1. Lift coprime factors one π\piπ-adic digit at a time and compare finite-level counts.
  2. At a degree-δ\deltaδ point, select a block over OδO_\deltaOδ​ and descend its Frobenius conjugates; equal counts give Haar preservation.

Proof. For coprime monic residue factors GjG_jGj​, including their multiplicities, fix every leading coefficient to be one. At an additional π\piπ-adic digit, multiplication linearizes to

(hj)j⟼∑jhj∏i≠jGi. (h_j)_j\longmapsto\sum_j h_j\prod_{i\ne j}G_i. (hj​)j​⟼j∑​hj​i=j∏​Gi​.
(7.2)

Reduction modulo GjG_jGj​ proves injectivity, because deg⁡hj<deg⁡Gj\deg h_j<\deg G_jdeghj​<degGj​ and the other factors are units modulo GjG_jGj​. Source and target have dimension nnn, so the map is bijective. For homogeneous factors normalize one nonzero residue coefficient in each factor and in the product. Take the target modulo the scalar direction of ∏Gj\prod G_j∏Gj​. A kernel element then has Gj∣hjG_j\mid h_jGj​∣hj​ for every jjj; equal degrees make hjh_jhj​ a scalar multiple of GjG_jGj​, and its zero normalization coordinate makes it zero. Again the dimensions are nnn. Successive unique digit lifting proves the factorization bijection modulo every πν\pi^\nuπν, then over OOO by completeness. There are qδjrj(ν−1)q^{\delta_jr_j(\nu-1)}qδj​rj​(ν−1) lifts in each factor cell and qn(ν−1)q^{n(\nu-1)}qn(ν−1) in the product cell. These bijections preserve uniform counting measure, so preserve Haar measure on cylinder sets and hence on Borel sets.

For one degree-δ\deltaδ residue polynomial ggg, pass to OδO_\deltaOδ​. Its distinct residue roots separate the grg^rgr cell into coprime blocks. The Frobenius generator of Gal⁡(Kδ/K)≃Gal⁡(kδ/k)\operatorname{Gal}(K_\delta/K)\simeq\operatorname{Gal}(k_\delta/k)Gal(Kδ​/K)≃Gal(kδ​/k) permutes them transitively. Selecting the block above one fixed root is a bijection: the inverse multiplies that block's Frobenius conjugates. Frobenius-invariant coefficients lie in OOO, also modulo πν\pi^\nuπν; this follows digit by digit from the π\piπ-adic expansion with the unique representatives satisfying aqδ=aa^{q^\delta}=aaqδ=a, which Frobenius raises to the qqqth power while fixing π\piπ. These representatives lift uniquely because the derivative is congruent to −1-1−1 modulo π\piπ. Both finite-level cells have qδr(ν−1)q^{\delta r(\nu-1)}qδr(ν−1) elements, so the selected block is uniform. Translation by a fixed lift of its root has an integral triangular coefficient matrix with determinant one, and identifies it with (7.1) over OδO_\deltaOδ​. The point at infinity is rational and is treated by reversing the affine coordinate.

A root field of the original block contains this unramified extension: lift a root of the separable residue polynomial by Hensel inside its integer ring, a complete DVR [Ne99]. Relative to the extension its ramification index is unchanged and its residue degree is divided by δ\deltaδ. This proves precisely the operation ψδ\psi_\deltaψδ​ and the conditional product law.

There are qnq^nqn monic residue polynomials. Nonzero binary residue forms modulo scalars correspond to effective degree-nnn divisors on Pk1\mathbb P^1_kPk1​, with (qn+1−1)/(q−1)=[n+1]q(q^{n+1}-1)/(q-1)=[n+1]_q(qn+1−1)/(q−1)=[n+1]q​ classes. All these cells have equal measure. At every precision each normalized projective lift has the same number of unit-scalar preimages, so this assertion holds for the projective model specified in Section 1. ∎

The global discriminant locus is Haar-null. Indeed a nonzero polynomial on OmO^mOm has a null zero set, by induction on mmm: outside the null locus where all coefficients in the last variable vanish, each fibre has finitely many zeros; apply Fubini. The discriminant is nonzero in every characteristic: over the prime field there is a separable polynomial of each degree, and homogenizing one also supplies a binary form with nonzero discriminant. In positive characteristic one may take an irreducible polynomial over the finite prime field; in characteristic zero one may take a product of distinct linear factors. Thus the global models give finite étale algebras almost surely.

(8.3)

Coefficients with respect to the basis Ec,h=YhXc\mathcal E_{c,h}=Y^hX^cEc,h​=YhXc are called normal coefficients. There are continuous algebra homomorphisms commuting with †\dagger† given by

(8.4)

The geometric series ∑j≥0(−V)j\sum_{j\geq0}(-V)^j∑j≥0​(−V)j is both inverses of 1+V1+V1+V when VVV has positive degree. Applying †\dagger† twice cancels its scalar. Anti-multiplicativity is the exponent identity ck+c+d+h+k−(c+d)(h+k)=(c+h−ch)+(d+k−dk)−dhck+c+d+h+k-(c+d)(h+k)=(c+h-ch)+(d+k-dk)-dhck+c+d+h+k−(c+d)(h+k)=(c+h−ch)+(d+k−dk)−dh. The remaining formulas in (8.3) follow from (8.1) by induction. The embeddings send (X,Y)(X,Y)(X,Y) to (J,Y)(J,Y)(J,Y) and (X,J)(X,J)(X,J), respectively. They do not lower degree. Their commutation with †\dagger† holds on X,YX,YX,Y and coefficients by (8.3), hence on products and on every truncation. ∎

10. Totally ramified fields and the Euclidean algorithm

A one-field monomial excludes products of nonconstant child laws; residue degree one also excludes nonrational tangent points. Only transitions supported at one rational point survive. Their crossing contacts follow the subtractive Euclidean algorithm, ending at a cluster indexed by their greatest common divisor. The totally ramified coefficient can therefore be computed from proper-divisor cluster data.

For a state sss of degree NNN, let τs=[ZN,1]Fs\tau_s=[Z_{N,1}]F_sτs​=[ZN,1​]Fs​, and put τ(n)=[Zn,1]Bn\tau(n)=[Z_{n,1}]B_nτ(n)=[Zn,1​]Bn​. Write A(n,1)A_{(n,1)}A(n,1)​ and R(n,1)R_{(n,1)}R(n,1)​ for the corresponding one-field probabilities. Global assembly immediately gives

τ(1)=1,A(n,1)=q1−nτ(n),R(n,1)=q+1[n+1]qτ(n). \tau(1)=1,\qquad A_{(n,1)}=q^{1-n}\tau(n),\qquad R_{(n,1)}=\frac{q+1}{[n+1]_q}\tau(n). τ(1)=1,A(n,1)​=q1−nτ(n),R(n,1)​=[n+1]q​q+1​τ(n).
(10.1)

Indeed a single type variable Zn,1Z_{n,1}Zn,1​ to the first power cannot arise from two occupied points, since each child law has positive degree and every one of its monomials contains a type variable. A nonrational point cannot produce residue degree one. Only one rational point of multiplicity nnn remains: there are qqq affine choices or q+1q+1q+1 projective choices.

11. Root moments, splitting, and unramified fields

Root counts must retain products of fields while ignoring every factor except (1,1)(1,1)(1,1), so the one-field extraction cannot compute them. A type-variable substitution can retain each rational root without rejecting the other branches.

Appendix A. Passing to the formal exceptional line

Independence on the formal exceptional line requires compatible finite-level gluings to survive completion. Degreewise surjectivity lets cochains lift, but cohomology can still acquire an inverse-limit cokernel. Eventual surjectivity on sections removes that obstruction and gives the formal-limit assertion of Lemma 4.1.

On the two affine charts and their affine intersection, sections of a coherent sheaf restrict surjectively from level j+1j+1j+1 to jjj, by affine exactness for the quasi-coherent kernel. The completed Čech complex is their termwise inverse limit. The formal affine pieces are acyclic: lift a primitive (a cochain whose Čech differential is the given cocycle) of a finite-level cocycle successively, correcting each discrepancy by a primitive in the exact affine complex of the kernel sheaf. The level-jjj correction lies in the kernel IjF/Ij+1F\mathcal I^j\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{j+1}\mathcal FIjF/Ij+1F, hence lifts into IjF\mathcal I^j\mathcal FIjF; these corrections therefore converge in the defining topology. Hence this two-chart complex computes formal cohomology and has no degree-two term.

For a tower of complexes Cj∙C_j^\bulletCj∙​ with surjective transition maps rjr_jrj​ in each degree, the map Δ(c)j=cj−rj(cj+1)\Delta(c)_j=c_j-r_j(c_{j+1})Δ(c)j​=cj​−rj​(cj+1​) on ∏jCj∙\prod_j C_j^\bullet∏j​Cj∙​ is surjective: choose c1c_1c1​ and solve successively for cj+1c_{j+1}cj+1​. Its kernel is the inverse limit. The resulting cohomology sequence gives (4.2). If the H0H^0H0 maps are eventually surjective, the first cokernel vanishes: solve on the surjective tail, then solve the finite initial segment backward. This removes the inverse-limit obstruction asserted in Lemma 4.1. ∎

Appendix A (passing to the formal exceptional line) covered by lemmas confidence: low

As for Lemma 4.1: only the finite-level Čech statements are formalized (surjective reductions, stabilization, threads); there is no formal completion in the Lean development.

In the stable range d ≤ j + 1, the map induced by reduction between the cokernels of the twisted finite Čech differentials at levels j + 1 and j is a bijection.

theorem actual_twisted_coker_reduction_bijective (R : Type) [CommRing R] (t x : R)
    (hreg : RegularParameterPair R t x) (beta : BlowupRestriction R t x) (d j : ℕ) (hd : d ≤ j + 1)
    (hnext : cechInputLattice R t x (j + 1) ≤
      (cechOutputLattice R t x (j + 1)).comap (fullCechDifferential R t x beta d))
    (hnow : cechInputLattice R t x j ≤
      (cechOutputLattice R t x j).comap (fullCechDifferential R t x beta d))
    (hcomm : (cechOutputReduction R t x j).comp
        (finiteCechDifferential R t x beta d (j + 1) hnext) =
      (finiteCechDifferential R t x beta d j hnow).comp (cechInputReduction R t x j)) :
    Function.Bijective (twoTermCokerMap (finiteCechDifferential R t x beta d (j+1) hnext)
      (finiteCechDifferential R t x beta d j hnow) (cechInputReduction R t x j)
      (cechOutputReduction R t x j) hcomm)

How this was made

This paper and its formalization were made in October 2026 under the direction of Asvin G, who posed the problem, set the standards, and verified the main statements. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) wrote the informal proof of the type laws and of the reciprocity theorem, the Lean blueprint, and the text of the paper; Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic) orchestrated the work, ran the fresh-context adversarial reviews and revision rounds, and built this site. The Lean 4 proofs were produced from the blueprint by a fleet of Claude agents on the Prove2Me platform against a pinned Mathlib, then unified and golfed into the single codebase shown here; every main theorem was checked for axioms (propositional extensionality, classical choice, quotient soundness only) and statement preservation, with the certificates linked on the formalization page. Numerical checks of every displayed law against an independent implementation of the recursion accompany the text.
